name: Attack
desc: You make one attack with a weapon or an Unarmed Strike. Some features, such as Extra Attack, let you make more than one attack when you take this action. Certain spells and features also let you replace one of those attacks with something else.

name: Dash
desc: You gain extra movement equal to your Speed for the rest of the current turn. If your Speed is 30 feet, for example, you can move up to 60 feet this turn if you Dash.

name: Disengage
desc: Your movement doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks for the rest of the current turn.

name: Dodge
desc: Until the start of your next turn, attack rolls against you have Disadvantage if you can see the attacker, and you make Dexterity saving throws with Advantage. You lose this benefit if you have the Incapacitated condition or if your Speed is 0.

name: Help
desc: You help another creature with a task or distract a foe. When you Help with a check, the creature you help gains Advantage on the next ability check it makes for that task before the start of your next turn. Alternatively, you can Help an ally attack a creature within 5 feet of you; the first attack roll that ally makes against that creature before your next turn has Advantage.

name: Hide
desc: You try to hide by making a Dexterity (Stealth) check. If you succeed, you have the Invisible condition while hidden. The condition ends if you make a sound louder than a whisper, an enemy finds you, you make an attack roll, or you cast a spell with a Verbal component.

name: Influence
desc: You urge a monster or an NPC to do something. Describe what you want, then the DM calls for a Charisma (Deception, Intimidation, Performance, or Persuasion) check, or another check if it fits. The DM sets the DC based on the creature's attitude and the request.

name: Magic
desc: You cast a spell that has a casting time of an action, or you use a feature or magic item that requires a Magic action to activate. If a spell has a longer casting time, you must spend that time taking the Magic action each turn, maintaining Concentration, to finish it.

name: Ready
desc: You prepare to act later. Decide what perceivable circumstance will trigger your reaction, and choose the action you will take in response — or choose to move up to your Speed. When the trigger occurs, you can either take your reaction then or ignore the trigger. A readied spell requires Concentration and is cast with your action, then released with your reaction.

name: Search
desc: You make a Wisdom check to look for something. Typical skills: Insight, Medicine, Perception, or Survival, as the DM decides.

name: Study
desc: You make an Intelligence check to recall or analyze information. Typical skills: Arcana, History, Investigation, Nature, or Religion.

name: Utilize
desc: You use a nonmagical object — pull a lever, throw a flask, or otherwise interact with something that requires an action. Many objects can be used with this action; the DM decides if a check is needed.

name: Opportunity Attack
desc: You can make an Opportunity Attack when a creature you can see leaves your reach. Use your Reaction to make one melee attack against the creature. The attack occurs right before the creature leaves your reach. You can also make one if a creature uses the Disengage action? No — Disengage prevents Opportunity Attacks.

name: Advantage and Disadvantage
desc: When you have Advantage, roll 2d20 and use the higher. When you have Disadvantage, roll 2d20 and use the lower. Advantage and Disadvantage cancel each other; if both apply, you roll 1d20. Multiple sources of the same don't stack.

name: Cover
desc: Half cover: +2 bonus to AC and Dexterity saving throws. Three-quarters cover: +5 bonus to AC and Dexterity saving throws. Total cover: you can't be targeted directly. The DM decides the degree of cover from obstacles.

name: Concentration
desc: Some spells require Concentration. You can concentrate on only one spell at a time. Concentration ends if you cast another Concentration spell, have the Incapacitated condition, or die. When you take damage, make a Constitution saving throw to keep the spell (DC 10, or half the damage if higher, maximum DC 30).

name: Critical Hit
desc: If you roll a 20 on the d20 for an attack roll, the attack hits regardless of modifiers or the target's AC, and you roll all the attack's damage dice twice and add them together, then add modifiers once.

name: Death Saving Throws
desc: When you start your turn with 0 Hit Points, make a DC 10 death saving throw (d20, no modifiers unless a feature says so). 10+ is a success, 9 or lower is a failure. Three successes: you become Stable. Three failures: you die. A 20 on the d20 gives you 1 Hit Point. A 1 counts as two failures. Damage at 0 HP causes one failure, or two on a Critical Hit.

name: Difficult Terrain
desc: Every foot of movement in Difficult Terrain costs 1 extra foot. This is cumulative with other extra costs, such as crawling or climbing, unless a feature says otherwise.

name: Grappling
desc: You can replace one of your attacks with an Unarmed Strike to grapple. The target must be no more than one size larger than you and within your reach. The target makes a Strength or Dexterity saving throw against a DC of 8 + your Strength modifier + your Proficiency Bonus. On a failure, it has the Grappled condition.

name: Unarmed Strike
desc: Instead of dealing damage, you can use an Unarmed Strike to Grapple or Shove. Damage is typically 1 + your Strength modifier Bludgeoning. Shove: the target makes a Strength or Dexterity save (DC 8 + Str mod + PB); on a failure you knock it Prone or push it 5 feet.

name: Surprise
desc: If a combatant is surprised, they can't take an action, a Bonus Action, or a Reaction on their first turn of combat, and they have Disadvantage on their Initiative roll. After that turn, they are no longer surprised.

name: Initiative
desc: At the start of combat, every participant rolls Initiative: a Dexterity check (d20 + Dexterity modifier, plus any Initiative bonus). The DM ranks them from highest to lowest. That order stays for the fight. Ties: the DM decides the order, or the tied players agree.

name: Bonus Action
desc: You can take one Bonus Action on your turn only if a feature, spell, or other rule says you can. You choose when to take it during your turn unless the timing is specified. You can't take more than one Bonus Action on a turn.

name: Reaction
desc: A Reaction is an instant response to a trigger. You can take one Reaction per round. You can take it on another creature's turn. After you take a Reaction, you can't take another until the start of your next turn.

name: Rests
desc: A Short Rest lasts at least 1 hour of light activity; you can spend Hit Point Dice at the end. A Long Rest lasts at least 8 hours, including 6 hours of sleep. You regain all Hit Points and spent Hit Point Dice, plus features that recharge on a Long Rest.

name: Short Rest
desc: A Short Rest is a period of downtime at least 1 hour long, during which you do nothing more strenuous than eating, drinking, reading, and tending wounds. You can spend one or more Hit Point Dice at the end of it, rolling each die and adding your Constitution modifier.

name: Long Rest
desc: A Long Rest is 8 hours or longer. You must sleep for at least 6 hours. At the end, you regain all lost Hit Points and all spent Hit Point Dice. You also regain spent features that recharge on a Long Rest. If the rest is interrupted by 1 hour or more of walking, fighting, or similar, it is ruined.

name: Lightly and Heavily Obscured
desc: A Lightly Obscured area (dim light, patchy fog, moderate foliage) imposes Disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight. A Heavily Obscured area (darkness, opaque fog, dense foliage) is opaque — creatures in it have the Blinded condition when trying to see something there.

name: Hiding
desc: The DM decides when circumstances are appropriate for hiding. You need cover or an obscured area, and you can't hide from a creature that can see you clearly. Make a Dexterity (Stealth) check; that total is the DC for Wisdom (Perception) checks to find you, or is compared to passive Perception.
